title: Dxun, the Demon Moon
text: Largest of the four moons turning around Onderon, Dxun wears its jungle like a shroud. Storms roll in without warning, and the things beneath the canopy have never needed a reason to hunt. Settlers who came for timber stayed as bones. Those who came for the Sith stayed longer than they meant to.

title: The Green Dark
text: Light reaches the forest floor only in fractured shafts. Above, drexl wheel through ferns the height of towers. Below, mud swallows boots and root-arches drip with rot. The jungle is not hostile by intent. It is simply hungry, and it has grown hungrier since the Dark Lords came to feed on its nexus.

title: The Black Spire
text: The tomb of Freedon Nadd stands alone on a hill above the valley, a spire of black Mandalorian iron that no vine has touched in four thousand years. A broad landing pad juts from its base. Scholars call its bare stone impossible. Those who have stood at its breach say the silence is listening.

title: Mandalorian Ruins
text: Here the Mandalorians held Dxun until Revan's assault broke their line. Bunkers sag into the mud and craters hold black water. Rusted wire hangs in the ferns, and under the moss, minefields still wait. The Guard Captain who keeps this camp has forgotten why he stays. He only knows the ground is his.

title: The Jungle Tomb
text: A lesser tomb hides among the roots, its door ringed by mines and perimeter sensors that wake at the slightest disturbance. Its old builders wanted no grave robbers. The priests who kept it sealed their secrets behind sensor codes, and the codes still answer to anyone who knows how to ask.

title: The Snare Clearing
text: A ship cannot come quietly to the Warren, so none do. The landing clearing is rigged with snares and crude mines. Listening devices hang in the canopy and scavenged turrets sleep in their pits. Anything that drops through the haze trips an alarm before its engines have cooled.

title: Iziz
text: Iziz rises behind massive walls, angular and proud, its brown facades capped with blue roofs and crowned by pyramid temples. The city was built to keep the jungle out. The gate is a bridge under turret fire and ray shields, and every citizen knows the beasts beyond the wall are only waiting.

title: The Royal Palace
text: The palace stands on a hill over Iziz, reached by a stone-and-steel ramp that climbs from the starport to the southern gates. Its throne room was moved to the rear in later years, but the hill remembers the old tyrant. Ray shields hum across the stairs, and the turrets are polished for every new queen.

title: Onderon
text: Onderon is a temperate world of green plains and walled cities, a place that might have been peaceful if the moon in its sky did not bring the beasts. Its people fortified every town against Dxun's hunters, and its royal houses were built of the same stone and the same fear.

title: The Warren
text: Beneath the roots of an ancient temple, Rathatri made his home. Not the grand tomb of Nadd, but the scrap-lined crypts above it, where cracked statues watch and burial niches hold sleeping killers. He chose it for its hidden door, its narrow throats and the dark tricks still whispering in its walls.

title: Cannok
text: The cannok runs in bristling swarms through the undergrowth, breeding faster than the jungle can eat them. Alone, one is a nuisance. In a crowd of thirty, a cannok will swallow whatever fits in its jaws, and sometimes what does not. Zakkegs grow fat on them, and so do the scavengers who follow the zakkegs.

title: Maalraa
text: The maalraa stalks like a cougar and hunts like a ghost. It waits in the canopy for a wounded traveler to stumble past, then drops with a silent crash of leaves. Its claws can open armor seams. Those who survive the first leap rarely see a second, and the jungle keeps quiet about it.

title: Boma
text: The boma is a slow mountain of armored flesh, but it is not slow when its territory is breached. Mandalorians learned to fear its charge, and zakkegs learned to hunt its young. A tamed boma carries its rider through the storms like a living fortress, and its loyalty lasts only as long as the will that holds its reins.

title: Zakkeg
text: The zakkeg is the jungle's apex: a brown, thick-hided reptile with talons wider than a hand. It guards its territory like a sentry at a gate and does not share the ground. A zakkeg's ear is the proof of a kill, and its roar ends arguments among the scavengers.

title: Drexl
text: The drexl is a winged predator of purple scale, its males spanning twenty meters from tip to tip. Onderon's Beast Riders trained them as mounts, and a rider who holds the reins can cross the valley faster than any speeder. Bane once flew one from Dxun to Onderon, and few riders live to dismount.

title: Orbalisk
text: The orbalisk waits dormant in the caves, a cluster of dark shells like stones, until a host wanders close. Then it wakes. Thousands of tiny teeth grip the skin, and the thing spreads, smothering breath and light alike. Its shell can turn a lightsaber aside, and Nadd and Bane both wore it as armor.

title: Hunger Vines
text: Some of Dxun's plants learned to hunt when the dark side seeped into the soil. Their vines coil around anything warm, and their blossoms breathe a sweet mist that dulls the victim. Under Nadd's influence the jungle became a predator. Never walk beneath a flower on Dxun.

title: Holocron of Freedon Nadd
text: Nadd's holocron waits in the deepest chamber of his tomb, its facets dulled by four thousand years of stillness. Darth Bane found it and learned from its voice how to make the orbalisk armor. Whoever wakes it hears the old tyrant's promise of power first, and only later the price.

title: Orbalisk Armor
text: Plates of living-dark shell, grown and fitted to the body, that keep orbalisks from the face, hands and feet. Only Nadd and Bane are known to have worn it. The armor brings strength and healing, but it blinds the wearer to stealth and makes every shadow loud. Some say the shell can turn a blade aside.

title: Nadd's Short Lightsaber
text: In the sarcophagus at the back of the ritual chamber lies the short saber of Freedon Nadd, its hilt a black spine of Mandalorian iron. Its blade once burned a dull crimson. Whoever claims it is said to hear the old tyrant laughing as the crystal hums.

title: Mandalorian Iron
text: Smelted by hands that feared the Republic, Mandalorian iron resists blasters, fire and time. Nadd's tomb is built from it, and the wrecks in the Mandalorian ruins bear its scars. Smiths who learned to work it say the metal remembers every blow and refuses to forget the one that broke it.

title: Ward Stone
text: Sith ward stones ring the old temples, humming with power their makers understood and their successors only half remember. Rathatri has learned to coax them into snare fields and bursts of chaotic force, but never without risk. A ward that misfires can burn the hand that woke it, or the whole chamber around it.

title: Nadd's Dynasty
text: Freedon Nadd killed his master, Naga Sadow, and made himself tyrant of Iziz, bending the court to the dark side. He banished criminals beyond the walls to die in the jungle. Many did not die. They tamed the beasts, and the dynasty that thought it had buried its enemies found them waiting at the gates.

title: The Death of Naga Sadow
text: Naga Sadow taught Freedon Nadd the Sith arts, and Nadd repaid him with a blade. The apprentice carried his murdered master's lessons to Onderon and built a throne from them. Sadow's teachings were the reason Nadd was dangerous, and his killing was the reason Onderon bled.

title: The Beast Riders
text: Exiled to the jungle, the criminals of Onderon learned to speak with the beasts. They rode drexl across the sky and bomas across the plains. When the queen's soldiers hunted them, the Beast Riders answered. A raid took Princess Galia, and the Jedi who came to save her found the Kira fortress and the boma that led them there.

title: The Second Tomb
text: After Nadd's worshippers were destroyed in 3998 BBY, Jedi Master Arca Jeth moved the Dark Lord's tomb from its cavern beneath the palace of Iziz to the jungle moon Dxun. Nadd lies there with his queen, Amanoa, and his king, Ommin. The new tomb was built to contain his remains and the dark side that still clung to them.

title: Exar Kun's Breach
text: Exar Kun came to the tomb in search of forbidden knowledge and cut a wound in its outer wall with his lightsaber. The iron of the wall is nearly unbreakable, yet he cut through it. Scholars still argue whether he came a year after sealing or much later. The breach is still open, and it still smells of smoke.

title: The Battle of Dxun
text: The Mandalorians made Dxun a fleet command post and sowed its valleys with mines, turrets and traps for decades. When Revan's armies came, the jungle fought beside the defenders. Meetra Surik's line charged across a minefield and lost most of its soldiers. The Republic lost ten for every Mandalorian, the Mandalorians said. The craters still answer.

title: Bane in the Tomb
text: Darth Bane came to the tomb of Freedon Nadd and found what the Dark Lord had left behind: a holocron and a nest of orbalisks. He took both, and the armor he made from the shells changed him. What one master leaves to rot, the next master takes up. He took a drexl as well, and flew it to Onderon.

title: Vaklu's Revolt
text: General Vaklu, cousin to Queen Talia, wanted Onderon free of the Republic, and he had found friends among the Sith. He declared martial law in Iziz and sent his soldiers against the palace to finish his cousin. He failed and was imprisoned. The Sith had bargained with him for the tomb of Nadd.

title: The Dark Lord's Last Vigil
text: In 3951 BBY the loyalists of Darth Nihilus held the tomb of Freedon Nadd, and Onderon's general had promised them the road. They built their power in the spire's shadow until Meetra Surik's companions came up through the jungle and broke them at its doors. The valley has been quiet since, though nothing living there is at peace.

title: THE STARVING BEAST
text: The first trial has no teacher. Recruits are left in the deep jungle with a knife, a day's water and one instruction: come back to the temple. Dxun does the rest. Those who return have learned the only lesson that matters here. Everything that lives is either hunting or being hunted, and hesitation decides which.

title: THE HOLOCRON OF TRAYA
text: A pyramid of cracked crystal that wakes in a ghost of grey robes and a voice like a blade drawn slowly. She calls herself Traya, and sometimes Kreia, and she does not teach. She asks questions until the answers cut. Every lesson she gives has a price, and she never says what it is until it has been paid.

title: THE RUMOR
text: A Sith Lord who is seen is a Sith Lord who is hunted. Every witness, every holo-recording, every hunter who walks away alive is a thread back to Dxun. Pull enough threads and the Republic sends commandos, then Jedi, then the Battlemaster himself. Silence the rumor, or be ready to meet what it brings.
